info.name: TaskForge — API & Feature Tests
info.description:
# TaskForge — API Explorer & Reviewer Feature Tests

✅ QUICK START
1. Start the API/database from https://github.com/Arvence/TaskForge: run ./setup.ps1; check http://localhost:8275/api/ready for Ready.
2. Import THIS ONE Postman Collection JSON. No environment file required: baseUrl and all test variables are collection-scoped. IMPORTANT: deselect any unrelated Postman environment to avoid variable shadowing.
3. API Explorer: send requests independently to inspect actual TaskForge endpoints.
4. Feature Tests: choose ONE scenario folder → Run folder → run in displayed order with 1 iteration and NO additional delay/concurrent workers; review assertions in Postman test results. Each test uses fresh application/key and its own identifiers.
5. Advanced Verification: guided read-only HTTP checks, with boundaries explained. True concurrent races, timeout determinism, and worker process crashes belong in .NET integration tests.

🟢 PASS = expected status AND payload/identity assertion. 409/404/415 may be expected passes in negative scenarios.
⚠️ STATEFUL: don't Run entire collection. Some requests acquire/cancel/replay jobs. Run ONE Feature Test folder at a time; never let another worker consume its generated applicationId. The priority scenario leaves 4 acquired attempts in server state: they will time out and be maintained, but no matching workers should execute them.
⚠️ WAIT: Automatic Retry includes an acquisition wait up to 20 seconds. Use Postman Agent timeout >25 seconds. Jobs are created but no business handlers are run by Postman.
⚠️ SECURITY: TaskForge API intentionally has no auth: run on a trusted network. Never expose it publicly without access control.
⚠️ ENVIRONMENT: If your Postman environment defines baseUrl/applicationId/workerId, its values override collection variables. Select "No Environment" for portable tests.
⚠️ EXPORT: More → Export collection (v2.1) to postman/TaskForge.postman_collection.json. Variables, saved response samples, scripts and folder descriptions travel with this one JSON file. Running server/database and run history do not.

API EXPLORER
01 Health & Discovery; 02 Jobs Submit & Inspect; 03 Jobs Lifecycle; 04 Executions Worker Protocol; 05 Legacy 410 Gone. The original 17 requests + 21 sample responses are preserved.
FEATURE TESTS (self-contained per folder)
01 Priority Scheduling: 4 submissions → 4 acquisitions asserting Critical, High, Normal, Low.
02 Idempotency: 201 new → 200 identical ID → 409 changed body/same key → 201 new key.
03 Automatic Retry: submit → acquire → fail → server backoff → new attempt → complete → attempt history.
04 Cancellation & Replay: cancel → replay with new ID; original unchanged.
05 Attempt Ownership: wrong worker rejected; valid completion and duplicate ack accepted.
06 Application Routing: app B has no compatible jobs; app A acquires its own job.
07 Validation & Errors: 400/404/415 negative cases.
ADVANCED VERIFICATION
01 Concurrent Workers, 02 Timeout & Recovery, 03 Worker Crash Recovery: read-only inspection and explicit .NET integration-test references, NOT purported proof by Postman Runner.

SOURCE OF TRUTH
https://github.com/Arvence/TaskForge/blob/main/docs/http-api.md
https://github.com/Arvence/TaskForge/blob/main/docs/architecture.md
https://github.com/Arvence/TaskForge/blob/main/docs/dotnet-client.md
Runtime OpenAPI: {{baseUrl}}/openapi/v1.json.
TaskForge executes business code in external client workers, NEVER inside its orchestration API.

item.name: 01 — Concurrent Workers

exec: // Informational inspection only; never treat this as proof of concurrency, timeout, or process crash recovery.

request.description: ⚠️ This GET only inspects job distribution. Sequential Postman requests do NOT prove two clients racing for the same job. Verify atomic SQL acquisition via TaskForge.IntegrationTests; client TaskForgeWorkerOptions.SlotCount controls parallel handlers.

item.description: ⚠️ Guided inspection only: sequential Postman acquisition illustrates distinct assignments, but does NOT prove simultaneous races. True atomic concurrency needs .NET integration tests; see repository tests.

01 — Inspect current job and retry states

item.name: 03 — Worker Crash Recovery

request.description: ⚠️ Readiness only confirms SQL connectivity. To prove crash recovery, stop an active worker process, allow lease+deadline recovery, start worker again, and inspect attempt history. See TaskForge integration tests.
